rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: They argue that calling the Qur’an hadith makes it temporally originated: hadith is recent rather than ancient, and its letters and words arise successively.
rows.anchor: القائلون بحدوث القرآن احتجوا بهذه الآية من وجوه

rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: They argue that a revealed thing occupies a locus subject to another’s control, so the Qur’an must be originated.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى وصفه بأنه نزله والمنزل يكون في محل تصرف الغير

rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: They infer that the superlative “best discourse” puts the Qur’an in the same genus as other discourse; since other speech is originated, so is it.
rows.anchor: قوله أحسن الحديث يقتضي أن يكون هو من جنس سائر الأحاديث

rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: They argue that kitab derives from gathering, implying a collected object subject to an agent’s disposal and therefore originated.
rows.anchor: وصفه بكونه كتابا والكتاب مشتق من الكتبة وهي الاجتماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi limits the argument to discourse composed of letters, sounds, words, and expressions, which he regards as created.
rows.anchor: نحمل هذا الدليل على الكلام المؤلف من الحروف والأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi divides the Qur’an’s excellence into two possible grounds: its wording and its meaning.
rows.anchor: الحديث بحسب لفظه أو بحسب معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s verbal excellence includes its eloquence and forcefulness.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ذلك الحسن لأجل الفصاحة والجزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its style is a distinct genre, unlike poetry, sermons, or letters, yet every sound nature finds it pleasant and delightful.
rows.anchor: القرآن ليس من جنس الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its meanings are excellent because it is free of contradiction; a book without contradiction is miraculous, as 4:82 argues.
rows.anchor: أنه كتاب منزه عن التناقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another aspect of its excellence is its extensive disclosure of unseen matters about the past and future.
rows.anchor: اشتماله على الغيوب الكثيرة في الماضي والمستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an contains a vast range of beneficial sciences, which Razi organizes through the creed and confession in 2:285.
rows.anchor: العلوم النافعة هي ما ذكره الله في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God’s essence includes knowing that God exists, is beginningless, and endures forever.
rows.anchor: معرفة الذات فهي أن يعلم وجود الله وقدمه وبقاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God must be transcendent above being a substance, composite of parts, or confined to a place or direction; four Qur’anic negators express this transcendence.
rows.anchor: وهو كونه جوهرا ومركبا من الأعضاء والأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an teaches God’s positive attributes, including creative power, omniscience, life, will, hearing and sight, speech, command, mercy, and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: فأولها العلم بالله ، والعلم بكونه محدثا خالقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine acts concern spirits, which few can know, and bodies, divided into the higher and lower worlds.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن الأفعال إما أرواح وإما أجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the higher-world sciences are the heavens, sun and moon, lights, shadows, day and night, stars, Paradise, Hell, the Throne, the Kursi, the Preserved Tablet, and the Pen.
rows.anchor: البحث عن أحوال الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an describes Earth as a cradle, bed, receptacle for living and dead, subdued, and spread out for travel.
rows.anchor: وقد وصفها بصفات كثيرة إحداها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its lower-world sciences include the sea, air and winds, thunder, lightning, rain, clouds, plants and fruits, and animals.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الباب ذكر الصواعق والأمطار وتراكم السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It discusses human origins and the marvels of hearing, sight, speech, intellect, and understanding.
rows.anchor: عجائب تكوين الإنسان في أول الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It relates prophets, kings, and human history from creation through Judgment, then death, resurrection, and the states of the blessed and wretched.
rows.anchor: تواريخ الأنبياء والملوك وأحوال الناس من أول خلق العالم إلى آخر قيام القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi concludes that the Qur’an contains ten sciences of the heavens and ten of the elemental world, all elevated fields of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقد أشرنا إلى عشرة أنواع من العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an covers moral training, distinguishing virtues from vices, including justice, beneficence, giving to kin, and rejecting indecency, wrong, and aggression.
rows.anchor: فهو المسمى بعلم الأخلاق وبيان تمييز الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an contains the foundations of jurisprudence in the most complete form.
rows.anchor: وهو المسمى بعلم الفقه والقرآن مشتمل على جملة أصول هذا العلم على أكمل الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God’s beautiful names is another branch of knowledge about God.
rows.anchor: ولله الاسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an treats angels both summarily and in detail: as messengers and cosmic administrators, ranks of worshippers, Throne-bearers and attendants, keepers of Hell, recorders, and protecting angels.
rows.anchor: والقرآن يشتمل على شرح صفاتهم تارة على سبيل الإجمال وأخرى على طريق التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of angels can also extend to jinn and devils.
rows.anchor: وقد يتصل بأحوال الملائكة أحوال الجن والشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an discusses earlier scriptures, including Adam’s words and Abraham’s trial, as well as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
rows.anchor: شرح أحوال كتاب آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It names some messengers and leaves others unnamed, as 40:78 says.
rows.anchor: منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful accept that religious duties bind them, expressed in their words, “We hear and obey.”
rows.anchor: أن يقروا بوجوب هذه التكاليف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As disclosure of divine majesty deepens, worshippers see their shortcomings more clearly and ask forgiveness more often.
rows.anchor: كانت المكاشفات في تقصير العبودية أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in the return to God, resurrection, and Judgment is another essential body of religious knowledge.
rows.anchor: معرفة المعاد والبعث والقيامة وهو المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is an inexhaustible sea of essential religious teachings; no other book contains this full range, and Razi’s own commentary captures only a drop.
rows.anchor: القرآن بحر لا نهاية له في تقرير هذه المطالب وتعريفها وشرحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi directs readers to his earlier explanation of “the Book” at 2:2.
rows.anchor: ذالك الكتاب لا ريب فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the whole Qur’an is mutashabih because its parts resemble one another.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه يشبه بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike long books that vary in eloquence, every part of the Qur’an is fully eloquent.
rows.anchor: والقرآن يخالف ذلك فإنه فصيح كامل الفصاحة بجميع أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated accounts, such as the story of Moses, remain equally eloquent throughout the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: حكى قصة موسى عليه السلام في مواضع كثيرة من القرآن وكلها متساوية متشابهة في الفصاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its signs and explanations reinforce and confirm one another.
rows.anchor: كل ما فيه من الآيات والبيانات فإنه يقوي بعضها بعضا ويؤكد بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its many sciences share one purpose: calling people to religion and establishing God’s majesty, including in every narrative.
rows.anchor: متشابهة متشاركة في أن المقصود منها بأسرها الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathani points to paired patterns throughout the Qur’an: command and prohibition, general and particular, concise and expanded, heaven and earth, Paradise and Hell, darkness and light, and many other pairs.
rows.anchor: أكثر الأشياء المذكورة وقعت زوجين زوجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These pairs show that all things besides the Real are subject to an opposite; only God is the one, unique, and absolute.
rows.anchor: كل ما سوى الحق زوج ويدل على أن كل شيء مبتلى بضده ونقيضه وأن الفرد الأحد الحق هو الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qashʿirīrah is a shiver-like change in the skin caused by awe and fear.
rows.anchor: تأخذهم قشعريرة وهي تغير يحدث في جلد الإنسان

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say that hearing verses of mercy and beneficence brings joy and softens hearts toward God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم عند سماع آيات الرحمة والإحسان يحصل لهم الفرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowers say that seekers at the beginning of reverence are overwhelmed by contemplating divine majesty but revived by glimpsing divine beauty.
rows.anchor: إن المحققين من العارفين قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on proofs that God is beyond location and direction can make the skin shiver because conceiving a being neither inside nor outside, connected nor separate from the world is difficult.
rows.anchor: الدلائل الدالة على أنه يجب تنزيه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contemplating God’s oneness and the divisibility of every spatial thing softens skin and heart toward remembrance.
rows.anchor: أنه يجب أن يكون فردا أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mind’s attempt to imagine pre-eternity fails because anything it pictures is finite; recognizing this limit produces bewilderment and a shiver.
rows.anchor: كل ما استحضرته في فهو متناه والأزل هو الوجود المتقدم على هذه المدة المتناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reasoning from necessary and possible existence lets the mind apprehend God as beginningless and endless, bringing calm and softness toward remembrance.
rows.anchor: ههنا موجود والموجود إما واجب وإما ممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These states are not confined to hearing punishment and mercy verses; that is only an initial level, with unbounded further degrees.
rows.anchor: بل ذاك أول تلك المراتب وبعده مراتب لا حد لها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Qur’an portrays God’s friends shivering or softening during unveilings, without loss of reason or bodily convulsions; such disturbance would be satanic.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال : القرآن دل على أن أولياء

rows.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
rows.claim: In the Ihya, al-Ghazali asks why many people show ecstasy at poems about union and separation but not when hearing Qur’anic verses; he offers several excuses.
rows.anchor: الشيخ أبا حامد الغزالي أورد مسألة في كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Qur’anic mysteries make his skin shiver, hair stand, and heart feel awe, while love poems make him frivolous; he considers this the sound path.
rows.anchor: كلما تأملت في أسرار القرآن اقشعر جلدي وقف على شعري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love poems describe union, estrangement, hatred, and love appropriate to creatures; attributing these literally to God is unbelief, and only learned scholars can translate them into meanings fitting divine majesty.
rows.anchor: كلمات مشتملة على وصل وهجر وبغض وحب تليق بالخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker’s identity affects a text: the Qur’an is spoken by God through Gabriel and the infallible Messenger, while the poet is a lying, lustful advocate of immorality.
rows.anchor: القائل في القرآن هنا هو الله بواسطة جبريل بتبليغ الرسول المعصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls to truth and the straight path, whereas poetry follows falsehood and wandering, as 42:52–53 and 26:224–226 show.
rows.anchor: مدار القرآن على الدعوة إلى الحق

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives qashʿirīrah from qashʿ, a dried hide, plus an added r to make a quadriliteral; the idiom means skin contracts and hair stands from extreme fear.
rows.anchor: تركيبه من حروف التقشع وهو الأديم اليابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that skin and hearts soften as they arrive at God’s presence, a presence not perceived by sensory faculties.
rows.anchor: التقدير تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم حال وصولها إلى حضرة الله وهو لا يحس بالإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says remembrance of God rather than remembrance of mercy because the highest lover loves God for God’s own sake, not for a benefit distinct from Him.
rows.anchor: من أحب الله لأجل رحمته فهو ما أحب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse mentions only skin shivering in fear but both skin and heart softening in hope because disclosure is fuller in hope: good is intrinsically sought, evil only incidentally, and disclosure occurs in hearts and spirits.
rows.anchor: المكاشفة في مقام الرجاء أكمل منها في مقام الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the Book: it is God’s guidance, by which He guides the servant whose chest He first opened to receive it.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الكتاب وهو هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s misled person has a hardened, dark, dull heart incompatible with guidance and therefore has no guide.
rows.anchor: من جعل قلبه قاسيا مظلما بليد الفهم منافيا لقبول هذه الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says his school’s proof here, and the Muʿtazilite objections and replies, are the same as those discussed at 6:125.
rows.anchor: استدلال أصحابنا بهذه الآية وسؤالات المعتزلة وجوابات أصحابنا عين ما تقدم
